key_insight: Hyperspectral imaging can distinguish and spatially map donor and acceptor components in roll-to-roll slot-die coated organic photovoltaic active layers in real time.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical inline metrology route for quality control during scalable organic solar cell manufacturing, helping detect coating nonuniformity as it happens.
method: Inline hyperspectral camera on roll-to-roll slot-die coated P3HT/OIDTBR active layers
Multivariate curve resolution to separate spatial donor and acceptor contributions
Spectral fitting of P3HT absorbance to estimate exciton bandwidth and aggregation-related properties
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method reliably resolved the spatial distribution of donor and acceptor signals and mapped exciton bandwidth across the coating.
watch_item: Industrial deployment will depend on robust calibration, fast spectral processing, and tolerance to motion, lighting, and coating variability in continuous production.
paper_title: Hyperspectral imaging for inline quality monitoring of roll-to-roll slot-die coated organic photovoltaic active layers
